title: First 20 high-confidence Early Buddhist textual crosswalks
selection_rationale: This benchmark starts with Dīgha Nikāya because SuttaCentral explicitly reports that its DN and MN correspondences had been thoroughly checked for accuracy and completeness. Every selected work has at least one Chinese full parallel plus an independent non-Pāli Indic witness identified in the comparative source: Sanskrit manuscript fragments for 19 works, a Gāndhārī Mahāparinirvāṇasūtra witness for DN 16, and a cross-tradition Prākrit Paesi witness for DN 23.

epistemic_policy.reason: Independent recensions are not assumed to be verbatim. The dataset uses full_textual_parallel, partial_textual_parallel, fragmentary_textual_parallel, shared_passage, and doctrinal_parallel.
epistemic_policy.absent_witness_rule: not_identified_in_selected_sources means only that this benchmark did not identify a witness in its selected evidence set; it is not evidence of non-existence.
epistemic_policy.bhs_rule: No witness is labeled Buddhist Hybrid Sanskrit merely from linguistic appearance. Use bhs only when an edition or scholarly source explicitly supports that classification.

relation_classes.full_textual_parallel: Whole-discourse correspondence in the comparative source. The texts may still differ substantially in wording and content.
relation_classes.partial_textual_parallel: Markedly incomplete whole-discourse agreement; only a limited portion corresponds.
relation_classes.fragmentary_textual_parallel: A surviving manuscript fragment securely identified with the work/recension. This is orthogonal to full-vs-partial discourse correspondence.
relation_classes.shared_passage: A passage-level correspondence without a whole-discourse claim.
relation_classes.doctrinal_parallel: A conceptual/doctrinal similarity only; not evidence of textual descent by itself.
